summary: Handrio Nurhan specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned a BA at Soka University of America (2011–2015), an MA at Texas Tech University (2016–2018), and a PhD at Boston University (2018).
Hank Glassman works in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He has been affiliated with Haverford College, where he was attested as faculty in 2009 and 2019.

Hanna Havnevik is a scholar of Tibetology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. She served as Professor at the University of Oslo (attested 2006–2008) and later as Professor Emerita (attested 2026).
Hanna Wałkówska was an Indologist who studied at the University of Breslau (~1945–1950) under Ludwik Skurzak. She later held a post at the University of Breslau from ~1950 to 1991.

Hannah Gould works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. She studied at the University of Melbourne and University of Oxford, and held posts at Monash University, St Vincent's Hospital Melbourne, and the University of Melbourne (Lecturer, 2024).

Hannes Sköld was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Gothenburg and Lund University. He served at Lund University as Docent of Slavonic Languages (1920) and Docent of Comparative IE Linguistics (1926).

Hanns Oertel was an Indologist and linguist who earned his PhD at Yale under William Dwight Whitney. He held posts at Yale (1891–1917), Marburg (1922–1925), and Munich (1925–1935), among other positions.

Hanns-Peter Schmidt was an Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar and Indologist. After completing his PhD at the University of Hamburg under Ludwig Alsdorf, he held posts in India, Germany, and at UCLA (1965–2000).

Hans Adolf Dietrich Hartmann was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Marburg, Humboldt University (PhD 1933), and University College Dublin. He later served as Professor of Comparative IE Linguistics at the University of Hamburg (1953–1978).

Hans Conon von der Gabelentz was a scholar of linguistics, Sinology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Leipzig and Göttingen (1825–1828) and founded the Deutsche Morgenländische Gesellschaft.

Hans Delbrück was a historian and archaeologist who studied at the University of Bonn (~1868–1873). He held posts at Frederick William University Berlin (1885) and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1881–1921).
Hans E. Kauffmann was a scholar of history and archaeology. He studied under Robert von Heine-Geldern at the University of Vienna and earned his PhD from the University of Zurich in 1934.

Hans Frederik Hendriksen was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Copenhagen. He served as Professor of Sanskrit at Uppsala University (1947–1951) and Professor of Indian-Oriental Philology at Copenhagen (1951–1983).

Hans Haas was a scholar of religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies who studied at Erlangen-Nuremberg. He held posts at the University of Tokyo (~1900–1909), Jena (1913), and Leipzig (from 1915).

Hans Harder is an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied at Hamburg, Heidelberg, and Halle-Wittenberg (PhD under Rahul Peter Das; Habilitation). He was an assistant at Halle-Wittenberg (1995–2007).
Hans Hartog is an Indologist who studied at Tübingen, Kirchliche Hochschule Bethel, Munich, and Marburg, completing his PhD under Friedrich Heiler in 1939.

Hans Heinrich Schaeder was an Iranian studies and religious studies scholar who earned his PhD at Breslau. He held professorships at Königsberg (1926), Leipzig (1930–1931), Humboldt University (1931–1944), and Göttingen (1946–1957).

Hans Henrich Hock is a linguist and Indologist who studied at Northwestern and Yale (PhD under Warren Crawford Cowgill). He served as Professor of Linguistics and Sanskrit at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (~1982–2007).

Hans Jensen Jørgensen was an Indologist and linguist who earned his PhD at Kiel University under Emil Sieg in 1911. He was a scientific assistant at the Ethnological Museum of Berlin from 1912 to 1919.
Hans Josef Nolte was a linguist and Indologist who earned his PhD at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg (~1891–1894). He served as Director of Gymnasium Papenburg from 1904 to 1916.
